# LexiGrid — Feature Panel Report

**Date:** 2026-06-09  
**Generated by:** 13-agent debate panel (4 critics · 5 ideators · 3 debate judges · 1 synthesizer)  
**Input spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-09-lexigrid-design.md`

---

## Design Manifesto

LexiGrid is genuinely special because it solves the fundamental problem with word games: the **search-versus-build distinction**. Every Wordle clone, every Spelling Bee variant asks the player to find things in a pre-constructed space. LexiGrid asks the player to construct the space itself. That inversion transforms a passive puzzle into an active optimization problem — the question is not "what words are hidden here?" but "what arrangement makes this tile set most valuable?" That distinction is worth protecting above all else.

The design north star is **tactile intelligence** — the feeling of being a craftsperson who handles physical objects with weight and consequence, slowly building something beautiful and efficient from raw materials. Every decision should serve either the spatial optimization loop (live feedback, directional cues, score legibility) or the physical intimacy of the board game aesthetic (weighted tile placement, warm materials, handcrafted details). Features that import gamification scaffolding from the mobile-game industrial complex — XP bars, streak-saver lives, unlock gates — corrode the cozy artifact feeling that is LexiGrid's aesthetic moat.

The **strategic sequence**: ship the core loop with three high-leverage foundations first — direction-aware word highlighting (which solves the backwards/diagonal open questions and teaches the 8-direction mechanic without tutorial text), weighted tile placement physics (which makes every interaction feel like handling a real object), and the emoji grid share card (which transforms the current dead-end clipboard text into a visual artifact people actually want to post). These three together constitute the minimum viable LexiGrid.

## Detailed Entries

---

### #1 — Word Discovery Ink Bloom — Direction-Aware Path Highlighting
**Category:** Enhance Existing · **Score: 9.30**

When a valid word is detected, a warm amber ink wash expands from the first letter outward along the word's direction via CSS clip-path — sienna for vertical, golden-orange for diagonals, reversed wipe with a dotted border for backwards words. A small Unicode arrow badge (←, ↘, etc.) fades over the midpoint cell after 2 seconds. This simultaneously solves two critical open questions (backwards word indicator and diagonal indicator) and transforms every discovery into a tactile ink-on-parchment moment.

> **Key argument:** Live feedback IS the game — but feedback that cannot be read is just colored noise; directional ink bloom makes the 8-direction detection legible and learnable without a single word of tutorial text.

**Implementation:** In `game.js`, the word-detection result already returns `{word, cells[], direction}` — add a `directionClass` mapper (e.g. `'ink-h'`, `'ink-v'`, `'ink-diag-dr'`, `'ink-rev'`) and apply it to each cell's classList. In `style.css`, define `@keyframes` clip-path wipe per direction category using CSS custom properties. The arrow badge is a `::after` pseudo-element on the midpoint cell. *Watch out:* diagonal wipes require clip-path polygon math — pre-compute the polygon values for all four diagonal directions.

---

### #2 — Tile Thud Physics — Weighted Drop Animation
**Category:** Enhance Existing · **Score: 8.25**

On tile placement, a 3-frame CSS keyframe fires: `scale(1.15) → scale(0.92) → scale(1.0)` at 180ms ease-out, with a brief expanding box-shadow that snaps to recessed depth. On mobile, a Web Audio API low-frequency oscillator (~80Hz, fast 12ms decay) fires as a tactile thud. Tiles in the tray have a barely perceptible 0.5px vertical rest oscillation every 8 seconds, as if sitting on an uneven surface.

> **Key argument:** The cozy board-game illusion is broken the instant interaction feels frictionless and digital — a weighted drop with overshoot-and-settle physically encodes mass and is the difference between "fun toy" and "beautiful artifact."

**Implementation:** Define `.tile-drop` as a one-shot animation class added on `pointerup`/`touchend`, removed via `animationend` listener. Web Audio: `new AudioContext()`, `createOscillator()` at 80Hz, `createGain()` with `exponentialRampToValueAtTime` from 0.3 to 0.001 over 0.12s. Gate behind `if (window.AudioContext)` for Safari. The idle oscillation is a CSS animation on `.tray-tile` with `animation-delay` seeded from tile index to desync them.

### #3 — Emoji Grid Share — LexiGrid Visual Language
**Category:** Enhance Existing · **Score: 9.15**

Replace the plain-text clipboard output with an emoji grid: each cell maps to a colored square (🟫 plain, 🟨 word found, 🟧 designed puzzle word, ⭐ bonus cell activated), producing a 4×4 emoji block above the score line. Pure string construction — no server needed. Transforms a dead-end text share into a visual artifact that communicates board complexity, implies skill, reveals nothing about the solution.

```
LexiGrid · June 9 🔠
🟧🟨🟫🟧
🟨🟧🟨🟫
🟫🟨🟧🟨
🟧🟫🟨🟧
34/42 pts (81%) · 7 words
```

> **Key argument:** Wordle's emoji grid is the single most-copied viral mechanic in browser games because it simultaneously shares a result, shows effort, and spoils nothing — LexiGrid's 4×4 grid maps perfectly.

**Implementation:** In `game.js` after submit, iterate `gridState` and map each cell to an emoji. Join rows with `\n`. ~15 lines total. Test in iMessage and Discord — stick to `🟫🟨🟧⭐` which render consistently cross-platform.

### #4 — Undo Button with Board State Snapshot
**Category:** New Feature · **Score: 7.20**

A single Undo button (curved-arrow icon, below the grid alongside Reset) reverts the last tile placement or swap via a shallow copy of the previous grid state — not a full history stack. Undo is grayed out when no placement has occurred since load or since the last undo. Reset remains a separate button requiring a confirmation tap.

> **Key argument:** The absence of undo is a cognitive tax on experimentation — players who feel every move is permanent become conservative, directly undermining the optimization loop.

**Implementation:** Maintain `prevGridState = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(gridState))` before each placement. On undo click, swap states and re-render. Clear `prevGridState` to `null` after undo to prevent double-undo. Reset calls `confirm()` before executing. ~10 lines each.

### #5 — Locked Anchor Tiles
**Category:** New Feature · **Score: 7.70**

2–4 tiles arrive pre-placed on the grid and cannot be moved — shown with a darker inset gradient, slightly different cream-to-tan tone, and a subtle CSS padlock pseudo-element. Puzzle designers specify anchor positions in the puzzle data shape. Anchors can sit on bonus cells to create high-value targets or in awkward corners to increase difficulty.

> **Key argument:** Transforms LexiGrid from a blank-canvas puzzle into a constrained construction challenge — players immediately ask "what words can I build through this E in the corner?" rather than optimizing in a vacuum.

**Implementation:** Extend puzzle data with `anchors: [{row, col, letter}]`. On init, place tiles into `gridState` with `isAnchor: true`. In drag/drop and tap handlers, add guard: `if (cell.isAnchor) return`. Anchors excluded from the tray count.

### #6 — Direction Badge on Found Word Highlights
**Category:** Enhance Existing · **Score: 7.40**

When a word highlights, a compact Unicode arrow badge (←, ↘, ↗, etc.) appears centered on the word's midpoint cell as a CSS `::after` pseudo-element in a small mahogany pill, then fades after 2 seconds. Directly answers the open question about communicating backwards and diagonal paths.

> **Key argument:** Without direction badges, players who discover a backwards or diagonal word cannot tell which cells are glowing for that word vs. an overlapping one — the badge makes the detection event legible.

**Implementation:** Tightly integrated with #1 Ink Bloom. Map each of the 8 direction enums to a Unicode arrow. Find midpoint cell: `Math.floor(cells.length / 2)`. Set `data-badge-arrow` on that cell; CSS `::after` reads `attr(data-badge-arrow)`. Remove attribute after 2000ms. Consider these a unified system with #1.

### #7 — Puzzle Completion Postcard — Results Screen as Artifact
**Category:** New Feature · **Score: 8.55**

The Results screen renders as a styled postcard: warm parchment rectangle with double-border, a pure-CSS geometric stamp in the top-right, the puzzle title in italic Georgia at a slight CSS rotation, the emoji grid share block as the central visual, and the score in monospace with subtle per-character CSS transforms suggesting typewriter misalignment.

> **Key argument:** The clipboard share text solves the mechanical sharing problem but not the emotional one — a postcard transforms the result into an artifact someone would share for its own beauty, not just the score.

**Implementation:** `<div class='postcard'>` with `background: #f5e6c0`, double border, `transform: rotate(-0.5deg)`. Stamp as `clip-path: polygon(...)` for perforated edge. Typewriter score uses individual `<span>` elements with `transform: rotate(Xdeg) translateY(Ypx)` seeded from puzzle ID (deterministic). ~60 lines new CSS, no image files.

---

### #8 — Seasonal Board Skin System — Passive CSS Theme Tokens
**Category:** Enhance Existing · **Score: 7.95**

Eight CSS custom properties (`--board-bg`, `--tile-face`, `--tile-shadow`, `--accent-warm`, `--ink-bloom`, etc.) are overridden by a `data-season` attribute on `<body>`. Four skins: **Summer** (honey oak, bright cream), **Autumn** (deep walnut, burnt-orange accent), **Winter** (pale birch, frost-white tiles), **Spring** (cherry wood, blush-tinted cream). Active skin auto-selected by month, stored in localStorage for manual override.

> **Key argument:** Seasonal variation tells players the game is alive and maintained without requiring new content — Autumn screenshots look dramatically different than Summer ones, making each share card feel like a moment in time.

**Implementation:** Four `[data-season='autumn'] { --board-bg: ...; }` blocks in `style.css`, ~8 variable overrides each (~35 lines total). On load: compute season from `new Date().getMonth()`, check localStorage override. Zero performance cost, zero new assets.

### #9 — 30-Second Animated Primer — No-Text Micro-Tutorial
**Category:** New Feature · **Score: 7.05**

On first launch, a 5-step silent animation plays over a dummy 3×3 grid: (1) tile drops onto grid, (2) adjacent tile forms a word, (3) a backwards word lights up with arrow badge, (4) a diagonal word lights up, (5) tiles rearrange and score jumps. Each step holds 1.2s. "Got it — Play" button skips at any point. Driven entirely by CSS animations on hardcoded demo elements — no game engine involvement.

> **Key argument:** The 8-direction rule is spatially invisible until someone sees it — text instructions cannot convey it as fast as watching backwards and diagonal words light up.

**Implementation:** Gate on `localStorage.getItem('lexigrid_tutorialSeen')`. The primer is a separate `<div id='primer'>` with a hardcoded 3×3 demo grid of static divs. CSS `@keyframes` sequences drive each step via `animation-delay` offsets. ~80 lines CSS, ~20 lines JS. `display:none` after seen.

### #10 — Ghost Replay — Yesterday's Best Path
**Category:** New Feature · **Score: 7.35**

After submitting, a "Show Best Solution" button plays back a pre-baked animated sequence of tile placements at 600ms intervals — tiles slide from tray to grid, each word highlights as it completes, score ticker climbs to maxScore. The replay is stored as an ordered tile-placement array in the puzzle JSON — no live computation at runtime.

> **Key argument:** The post-game currently ends in a dead end — Ghost Replay transforms it into a learning moment where players watch the ghost and think "I never would have tried ZEAL going diagonally there."

**Implementation:** Extend puzzle data with `solution: [{tileIndex, toRow, toCol}]`. `playGhostReplay()` iterates with `setInterval` at 600ms, calling the same `placeTile()` function with `isReplay: true` flag. Disable user interaction during replay (`pointer-events: none`). Puzzle designer authors the array once — the designer mode (see #11) should generate it. ~60 lines in `game.js`.

### #11 — Puzzle Authoring Workflow — Designer Mode
**Category:** New Feature · **Score: 7.90**

A hidden route (`?design=1` URL param or long-press title for 2s) opens a designer panel: pick grid size, type target words, click cells to assign bonus cell types, name puzzle and set difficulty. The tool validates all designed words are reachable with the given letters, computes `maxScore` programmatically, and outputs copyable JSON for `puzzles.js`. Entirely client-side.

> **Key argument:** User-generated content is the highest-leverage retention mechanic — it converts players into creators — and it simultaneously fixes the dangerous manually-entered `maxScore` field that critics flagged as the most likely trust-breaking bug in the current spec.

**Implementation:** `if (new URLSearchParams(location.search).has('design')) showDesignerPanel()`. Designer panel is a separate DOM section with textarea for word list, clickable grid for bonus cell assignment, difficulty selector. `computeMaxScore()` runs the same word-detection engine against the authored arrangement. Output via `JSON.stringify(puzzleObj, null, 2)`. ~150 lines `game.js`, ~40 lines `style.css`.

### #12 — Coffee Ring Easter Egg
**Category:** New Feature · **Score: 7.35**

A faint brown ellipse — CSS `radial-gradient` with a thin dark ring and transparent center, ~80px diameter — painted on the table surface CSS background, slightly off-center upper-right. Position seeded from puzzle ID so it shifts subtly between puzzles. On desktop hover, tooltip whispers: "Someone was here." Never interactive, never explained.

> **Key argument:** The coffee ring is the single sharpest signal that a human made this — board games accumulate life, and this Easter egg encodes that history at near-zero implementation cost with outsized emotional reward for the player who notices it.

**Implementation:** Add CSS custom props `--coffee-x` / `--coffee-y` to `.game-wrapper`. Stack an additional `radial-gradient(ellipse 42px 35px at var(--coffee-x) var(--coffee-y), transparent 68%, #3a1f08 72%, transparent 76%)` on the existing oak gradient. In `game.js` on puzzle load, compute position: `const seed = parseInt(puzzle.id); const x = 55 + (seed % 7) * 4;` — deterministic, no random. Tooltip is a `title` attribute on the wrapper.

### #13 — Handwritten Puzzle Dedication Line
**Category:** New Feature · **Score: 6.75**

Each puzzle in `puzzles.js` gains an optional `dedication` field (max 60 chars) that appears at the very bottom of the game screen in faint, slightly-rotated italic Georgia at 35% opacity, as if penciled below the board. Fades in 3 seconds after load. On the Results postcard, the dedication appears in the message area. Examples: *"For M., who always finds words I miss."* · *"Puzzle 14 — summer solstice."*

> **Key argument:** A dedication line in pencil italic encodes that this puzzle was made by someone for someone — the kind of detail that shows up in reviews as "I don't know why but it feels warm."

**Implementation:** ~8 lines JS, 8 lines CSS. `.dedication { font-style: italic; font-size: 11px; transform: rotate(-0.8deg); color: #3d2010; opacity: 0.35; }`. Fade-in via `setTimeout`.

### #14 — Full Keyboard Navigation
**Category:** Enhance Existing · **Score: 5.95**

Arrow keys move focus between grid cells; Tab cycles tray tiles; Space selects/places; Escape deselects; Delete returns placed tile to tray. 3px amber focus ring always visible, never suppressed, using CSS `outline` (not `border`) so it renders outside the 3D box-shadow.

> **Key argument:** Keyboard navigation serves assistive technology users for whom it is non-negotiable, and power users for whom it is meaningfully faster once learned.

**Implementation:** `keydownHandler` on `document` maps ArrowKeys to `focusedCell` index variable. Use `:focus-visible` not `:focus` to avoid showing ring on mouse click. Add `tabindex='0'` to all grid cells and tray tiles in the render loop. ~80 lines `game.js`.

---

### #15 — High-Contrast Mode Toggle
**Category:** New Feature · **Score: 5.85**

Small accessibility icon in the score bar toggles high-contrast mode via `data-hc` attribute on `<body>`. In HC mode: `#1a1a1a` background, white tiles, `#ffff00` word highlights, `#00ffff` for 2×L, `#ff8800` for 2×W — all WCAG AA. Preference persists in localStorage.

> **Key argument:** The warm amber-on-cream palette fails players with low vision or color blindness — warm amber on cream is particularly problematic, and a localStorage-persisted toggle means a player who needs it sets it once.

**Implementation:** `[data-hc='1']` block overrides the same CSS custom properties defined in the seasonal skin system (#8) — ~10 new lines of CSS. `toggleHC()` flips `document.body.dataset.hc`. Button is `<button aria-pressed>` in score bar.

### #16 — Tile Tray Grain Grouping — Weighted Visual Organization
**Category:** Enhance Existing · **Score: 6.35**

Tiles rendered grouped by point value: low vowels (1pt) on the left, consonants ascending toward the right. Within each group, tiles offset 1–3px vertically (seeded from puzzle ID, deterministic). A faint 1px pencil-line separator at 30% opacity divides vowels from consonants. Resolves the letter distribution open question with an aesthetic answer rather than a UI control.

> **Key argument:** In physical Scrabble, players manually sort tiles — this gives new players an implicit reading order without tutorial text, and the random vertical offset is critical: perfectly aligned tiles read as digital, offset tiles read as placed by a human hand.

**Implementation:** `trayTiles.sort((a, b) => LETTER_VALUES[a] - LETTER_VALUES[b])`. Apply `style.marginTop` from a seeded pseudo-random function (mulberry32 or lcg). Insert `<div class='tray-divider'>` between 1pt and 2pt+ groups. ~20 lines `game.js`.

### #17 — Streak Counter with Visual Streakcard
**Category:** New Feature · **Score: 7.35**

Track consecutive daily completions in localStorage `lexigrid_streak: {current, best, lastPlayedDate}`. Flame icon + count in score bar. Streak milestone banners at 3, 7, 14, 30 days. Share text appends `🔥 7-day streak` when current ≥ 3. A missed day resets to 0 with a gentle notification.

> **Key argument:** Loss aversion is the strongest retention hook in casual gaming — a player on a 14-day streak will return just to protect it — and "🔥 14-day streak" in a share card creates competitive pressure in the recipient.

**Implementation:** On daily submission: load streak from localStorage, compare `lastPlayedDate` to yesterday's ISO date. `[3,7,14,30].includes(current)` triggers milestone toast. Append streak to share string if `current >= 3`. ~40 lines.

### #18 — Anonymous "Others Also Found" Social Proof
**Category:** New Feature · **Score: 7.35**

Each puzzle gains an optional `bonusHints: ['WADE','DENS','RIFE']` array (words the designer discovered during testing that are valid in DICT but not in `puzzle.words`). After submit, Results screen shows: *"Other players also discovered: WADE, DENS, RIFE — did you find them?"* Static annotation, no server.

> **Key argument:** "Others found 3 more words you missed" directly triggers the competitiveness and completionism that drives word game players, extends engagement per puzzle, and creates a share moment.

**Implementation:** On Results render, check `puzzle.bonusHints` against `foundWords` Set. Render missed hints. If all found: "You found everything — including the bonus words! ⭐". ~15 lines JS, 8 lines CSS.

### #19 — First Word Celebration with Word Type Label
**Category:** New Feature · **Score: 6.85**

The first word found per session triggers a distinct celebration: found tiles ripple with warm golden shimmer (CSS keyframe, 600ms), and a floating label appears above the grid showing word + direction in plain English: *"CAT — forward →"* or *"FIRE — diagonal ↘"*. A single Web Audio chime plays. After the first word, subsequent discoveries use only the standard gold highlight.

> **Key argument:** The first word discovery is the pivotal moment that confirms the player understands the mechanic — amplifying it with a plain-English direction label teaches the direction vocabulary so subsequent directional badges are immediately legible.

**Implementation:** Check `sessionStorage.getItem('lexigrid_firstWordSeen')` in the word-detection callback. Add `.tile--first-shimmer` CSS class to found cells. Show `<div class='first-word-label'>` with `word + ' — ' + DIRECTION_LABELS[direction]`. Auto-dismiss after 2.5s. Chime: same Web Audio pattern as #2 but at ~880Hz with slower decay for a bell tone.

### #20 — Clarify Scoring De-Duplication Rules in Code
**Category:** Simplify/Clarify · **Score: 6.30**

The spec states "a word scores once regardless of direction" but edge cases are undefined: Does CAT forward and TAC backward count as one word or two? Does CATS in row 1 and CATS in column 2 score once or twice? These rules must be explicit before implementation — any post-ship patch that changes scoring rules will invalidate localStorage high scores and destroy player trust.

> **Key argument:** Score de-duplication ambiguity is a silent bug factory — any post-ship patch that changes how words are counted will alter every historical high score stored in localStorage, permanently breaking player trust.

**Implementation:** Document canonical rules as a block comment above `detectWords()` in `game.js`: (1) CAT and TAC are different words and both score independently; (2) the same string found via two different cell sets both score — use a `foundWordKeys` Set keyed by `word + ':' + cells.map(c=>c.row+','+c.col).join('|')` to deduplicate identical paths only. Write a minimal test suite covering these 4 edge cases before any puzzle is authored.

---

## Critic Panel Highlights

### What the critics agreed on
- **Keep live word feedback** — all 4 critics rated this the highest-impact decision. Non-negotiable.
- **Cozy aesthetic is a genuine differentiator** — do not drift toward flat/generic design under any pressure.
- **Daily + Library format is right** — the shared daily tile set is the competitive hook. Keep it.
- **Fix the `maxScore` field** — manually authored `maxScore` is a trust-breaking bug waiting to happen. It must be computed by the engine (see Designer Mode, #11).

### The Skeptic's sharpest findings
- **Scoring system may be too complex** for new players who will ignore all three layers and play by feel. Consider whether Scrabble letter values are strictly necessary, or whether word length alone is sufficient differentiation.
- **Dual input system doubles edge cases** — tap-to-select works everywhere; implement drag-and-drop as progressive enhancement only after tap is proven.
- **5×5 grid will break portrait layout** on phones — 25 tiles won't fit the tray without scrolling mid-puzzle. Defer 5×5 until the layout constraint is explicitly solved.

### The Viral Analyst's strongest recommendation
The share card currently has no URL. The game runs from `file://` but **nothing prevents hosting it statically** — GitHub Pages, Netlify, or itch.io require zero backend. Adding a URL to every share card transforms the share from a tombstone into an acquisition funnel. This is the highest-leverage single action for viral growth.
